title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: Saudi air links took another hit: Dammam airport was attacked on Wednesday night, and UAE airlines have now cancelled Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah flights through 24 October. At sea, Iran claims seven tankers were struck overnight, and only two container ships sailed into the Gulf last week.

stories.headline: Iran claims seven tankers hit overnight in the Gulf and Hormuz
body: Iran's IRGC Navy says four tankers doing ship-to-ship oil transfers in the northern Gulf were hit and caught fire, and three more struck mines west of the strait. UKMTO has not confirmed the claims, and no ships have been named. Trump accused Tehran of "faking hits" to push up oil prices.

What is new: the claims follow 12 UKMTO-logged attacks in the period to 16 October, including the container ship GFS Pride, which sank after an attack on 13 October. Only 254 ships crossed Hormuz in the week to 14 October, about 70% below prewar.
stories.soWhat: Whether or not every claim is true, carriers and insurers will price the risk. Keep war-risk surcharges on all Gulf sea cargo.

stories.headline: Only two container ships sailed into the Gulf last week
body: Drewry says just two container ships entered the Gulf in week 42, down from five the week before, as attacks keep disrupting vessel movements.
Its World Container Index rose 2% to $4,585 per 40ft on 22 October, the second weekly rise and the highest in 15 weeks. Shanghai–Rotterdam rose 3% to $3,632 and Shanghai–Genoa 5% to $4,152.
stories.soWhat: Very few boxes are getting inside Hormuz. East-coast ports and road links from Khor Fakkan and Fujairah carry the load, so that capacity is what we should be selling.

stories.headline: Dammam airport attacked; UAE airlines cancel Saudi flights through 24 October
body: King Fahd International Airport in Dammam was attacked on Wednesday evening. One person died and eight were injured, Saudi civil aviation said. Emirates has cancelled Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam flights, keeping only Madinah. Etihad has cancelled Dammam, Riyadh and Jeddah through 24 October, and flydubai cancelled Riyadh, Abha, Dammam and Ha'il on 22 October.

Freight is backing up. Expeditors says Emirates SkyCargo is trucking its backlog from Dubai World Central to Jeddah and Dammam. Riyadh customs clearance is suspended, with some cargo rerouted via Jeddah, and Jeddah port has landside delays of about 10–12 days.
stories.soWhat: New this week: Jeddah is now off UAE carriers too, and Riyadh customs is shut. Road from the UAE is the only dependable route into Saudi for now.

stories.headline: Gulf air capacity is still a fifth below prewar
body: WorldACD data for week 41 shows Gulf air cargo capacity fell 4% week on week, reversing a 4% rise the week before. It is still 20% below late February.
Global spot rates held at $3.55 per kg, up 34% on last year. Middle East and South Asia spot rates fell 2% and capacity fell 3%.
stories.soWhat: Tight Gulf lift keeps air yields firm. Hold our air rates and push customers toward booked space before peak.

stories.headline: Etihad Rail Freight runs about 250 trains a month to the east coast
body: Etihad Rail Freight has raised monthly train runs from about four to roughly 250 by moving rolling stock to serve Fujairah and Khorfakkan, its CEO said at the Sharjah Investment Forum. "We don't compete with trucks; we complement them," said Omar Alsebeyi.
The UAE also plans to make more than 5,000 products locally over the next decade, backed by a new AED 1 billion fund for smaller manufacturers.
stories.soWhat: Rail from the east coast is now real capacity. Build rail-plus-truck options into our Khor Fakkan and Fujairah inbound offer.

competitors.name: Emirates SkyCargo
competitors.headline: Suspends Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam and trucks the backlog
body: Emirates SkyCargo has suspended Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam through 24 October, with only Madinah operating. It is trucking backlog cargo from Dubai World Central to Jeddah and Dammam, per Expeditors' 21 October update.
Qatar Airways and Etihad have also suspended Riyadh and Dammam to the same date.
competitors.soWhat: The biggest belly and freighter player into KSA is now a road operator too. Our UAE–KSA trucking network is the edge, so sell it hard this week.

competitors.name: UPS
competitors.headline: UPS keeps its $1.50/lb UAE surge fee in place
body: UPS's surge emergency fee table, updated 15 October, still charges $1.50 per lb on US–UAE express shipments both ways and $1.34 per lb on other Middle East lanes, including Saudi Arabia. Both have been unchanged since 22 March and stay "until further notice".
UPS reports third-quarter results on 27 October.
competitors.soWhat: The integrators are not easing war surcharges. That is cover to keep ours, and a price point to beat on US lanes.

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: Aramex signs MoU with GMR Airports in India
body: Aramex has signed an MoU with GMR Airports covering GMR-run airports across India. The two will look at upgraded express cargo terminals with truck docks, screening, dedicated space and integrated customs.
A warehouse with direct airside access is targeted for March 2027, subject to a final agreement. Our latest financial figure is still record Q2 revenue of AED 1.83 billion, up 22%.
competitors.soWhat: India–UAE is one of our busiest express lanes. Faster clearance at GMR airports is a selling point for India–Gulf e-commerce accounts.

opportunities.title: Road into Saudi
opportunities.text: UAE airlines have cancelled Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam through 24 October, and Emirates is trucking its own backlog. Road express and FTL to KSA are in demand now.

opportunities.title: Jeddah instead of Riyadh customs
opportunities.text: Riyadh customs clearance is suspended. Offer clearance at Jeddah or at the land border with onward trucking to Riyadh.

opportunities.title: East-coast inbound by rail
opportunities.text: Etihad Rail runs about 250 trains a month to Fujairah and Khorfakkan. Pair rail with our trucking for inbound freight.

opportunities.title: Firm air yields
opportunities.text: Gulf air capacity is 20% below prewar and global spot rates are up 34% on last year. There is no reason to discount air.

opportunities.title: India–Gulf express
opportunities.text: The GMR MoU gives us a story for India–UAE e-commerce sellers ahead of peak.

watchouts.title: Saudi airport attacks
watchouts.text: Dammam was hit on 21 October and one person died. Flight cancellations could run past 24 October.

watchouts.title: Jeddah port delays
watchouts.text: Landside delays at Jeddah are about 10–12 days. Do not promise sea transit times into KSA without a buffer.

watchouts.title: Escalation at sea
watchouts.text: Iran claims seven tankers were hit. Even unconfirmed, it can lift war-risk premiums again.

watchouts.title: Gulf boxes almost stopped
watchouts.text: Only two container ships sailed into the Gulf last week. Jebel Ali-bound cargo faces long waits.

watchouts.title: UPS results on 27 October
watchouts.text: Another pricing and surcharge signal is due next week.

moves.title: Push UAE–KSA road capacity to air-stranded shippers
moves.text: Call key accounts with Saudi air cargo stuck by the cancellations. Offer road express and FTL from Dubai with a firm transit time.

moves.title: Reroute Riyadh shipments via Jeddah or the land border
moves.text: Riyadh customs is suspended. Set a default clearance path and tell customers before they book.

moves.title: Add a temporary KSA disruption surcharge on road
moves.text: Demand is jumping and capacity is finite. Price peak road capacity rather than absorbing it.

moves.title: Hold war-risk surcharges on Gulf sea cargo
moves.text: New attack claims and only two box ships into the Gulf last week. Keep surcharges and add delay clauses for Jebel Ali-bound cargo.

moves.title: Quote a rail-plus-truck inbound product
moves.text: Use Etihad Rail from Khor Fakkan and Fujairah with our last leg to Dubai and Abu Dhabi.

moves.title: Use the GMR deal in India–UAE pitches
moves.text: Brief the e-commerce sales team on faster India airport handling to win peak volume.

note: Read from today's news. Check against our own numbers before acting.
